properties.name: Final measurement for criterion 1: 177 of 180 tools in find_tools' top 5 (from 114 at baseline), held-out paraphrases 36 of 42 (from 16), three tools exempt at rank 6 with the reason, two scorer refinements refuted on the way
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-11 on the real server over stdio, both corpora, after every served tool carried a sentence stating its job in a user's words.

    find_tools top-5, main corpus (180)
      baseline (before #475)                         114
      after the scorer fix (#475)                    120
      first 37 phrasings                              152   ← and 19 of them failed the held-out check
      after rewriting those 19 + phrasing 26 more     177   (3 at rank 6, exempt with reason)
    held-out paraphrases (42, never consulted while writing)
      first phrasings                                  16
      after the rewrite                                36

⭐ THE HELD-OUT CHECK EARNED ITS PLACE ON THE FIRST PASS. Nineteen sentences passed the corpus and failed a paraphrase from a different angle — they had echoed the queries. Rewriting them from the tool's purpose in more than one register took the held-out set from 16 to 36 without touching the corpus, which is the difference between a sentence that was written and one that was tuned, measured.

WHAT MOVED OTHER TOOLS: giving 42 tools a user-register sentence pushed 26 others from the top 5 to ranks 6–10 — they now had competitors carrying the same plain words. Phrasing those 26 too closed all but three.

THE THREE EXEMPT, AND WHY THEY STAY: `consumption_report`, `governed_by`, `scan_nodes`, each at rank 6, each beaten by SHORTER descriptions on incidental words. Two scorer refinements were tried against both corpora: a 4-char floor on the name-prefix rule (so "all" stops matching `allocate`) was NEUTRAL at 177/36; a gentler length normalisation (len/600 for len/200) was WORSE at 174/34. Both were reverted — a change the corpus does not reward is noise — and the three are exempted in the acceptance test with a second test that fails if any of them climbs into the top 5 (a stale excuse) or drops out of the top 10 (a regression behind one).

SIX HELD-OUT MISSES REMAIN, and they are of two kinds: `detect_gaps` ← "what has nobody answered yet that I should chase the owner about", `loop_status` ← "what does the process still need from me" — the sentences were shortened to fit the 1,500-char budget and lost the words; and `complies_with` ← "satisfies the building code", `design_identity` ← "which project's model am I looking at" — a register the tool does not carry. These are the ceiling of word-matching on this surface and are stated, not hidden.

BOUNDS: both corpora by one author on one day, the held-out authored after the first phrasings (contaminated in the head if not on paper); one phrasing per tool per corpus; the acceptance bar is the default top 5 because that is what a consumer sees. The held-out set is deliberately NOT a CI gate, so it stays a check rather than the next thing tuned to.
